title: Deterministic aliasing & graceful rollback for tool-call interop
creator: Ravi Menon
description:
Problem: Customers run into brittle integrations when migrating from legacy function-based tool semantics (function name + positional args) to OpenAI-style tool descriptions (name + JSON schema). Name collisions, signature drift, and nondeterministic aliasing cause silent mis-routes and production errors.

Goal: Ship a thin compatibility gateway that deterministically resolves tool/legacy-function invocations, surfaces a safe migration path, and supports fast rollback when regressions are detected. The gateway should preserve streaming and structured output semantics and add minimal latency.

Proposal summary:
1) Deterministic aliasing: build an alias resolution engine that computes stable canonical IDs for tools using a fingerprint composed of (namespace, declared schema hash, last-known owner, stable slug). Avoid heuristic-only name mapping. The engine exposes an ordered list of candidate targets with an explicit match score and provenance metadata.

2) Signature-compatibility scorer: when multiple candidates exist, run a lightweight compatibility check between the incoming invocation payload and each candidate's stored signature (field presence, requiredness, type-family). Score by violations and use deterministic tie-breakers (owner priority, creation time). No probabilistic string-matching at decision time.

3) Greedy safe execution with soft-fallbacks: prefer exact matches. If the top candidate is not >= threshold, route to a sandboxed 'compat-run' that executes the invocation in a read-only/limited-calls mode and returns a guarded response to the caller plus a telemetry marker. This prevents silent mis-execution.

4) Rollback & canary plan: support simple rollout flags per-customer: off | canary | gradual | global. Canary runs for 1% of traffic with verbose telemetry and auto-rollback if error rate or semantic-failure rate exceeds configured SLOs.

5) Streaming and structured outputs: maintain streaming compatibility by ensuring we only swap in compatible codecs and chunking strategies. For structured outputs, the gateway validates JSON schema continuations and either patches missing fields or fails-fast based on policy.

Telemetry & observability: expose per-call provenance, match_score, candidate_list, chosen_target, fallback_mode, and signature_diff. Integrate with Console traces and per-token latency breakdown.

API changes and developer UX: add an admin REST endpoint to manage aliases/overrides and to view fingerprint histories. CLI tool (redwoodctl tool alias-explain) to help customers map legacy functions to OpenAI-style tools.

Backward compatibility constraints and performance: the resolution path must add <= 3ms median latency in the hot path. The sandboxed compat-run will be rate-limited and run on dedicated reserved capacity to avoid impacting primary runtime SLOs.

Testing and validation: unit tests for fingerprint determinism, integration tests exercising streaming passthrough, and long-running regression tests with recorded real-world invocation traces. Production canary with synthetic and customer-owned prompt sets.

Security review: the gateway inspects payloads and may touch PII; security review and KMS audit are required before Private/VPC rollout.
comments: 2025-02-11 - Lina Cho: Initial design draft posted. Key questions: what exact hashing algorithm for schema fingerprinting? Suggest sha256 over JSON canonical form. Action: Ravi to prototype hash function and collision tests.

2025-02-13 - Ravi Menon: Prototype committed: tools/compat/fingerprint v1. Uses canonical JSON (RFC8785) + sha256. Benchmarks attached: median fingerprint compute 0.18ms for 2KB schemas. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/3128
2025-02-14 - Security: flagged that sandboxed compat-run needs explicit KMS-scoped keys for any downstream webhooks. Marked security_review_required. Owner: Megan Park.
2025-02-15 - Lina Cho: Added rollback thresholds: error_rate > 1.5% OR semantic-failure > 0.8% triggers automated rollback. Need Console dashboard tile for semantic-failure rate.

2025-02-17 - Eng review (Kaveh Amini): Suggest deterministic tie-breaker order: (exact schema hash match) > (owner override) > (creation_time) > (alphabetical slug). Also request load tests for 100k QPS with cache hit/miss mix.

2025-02-18 - Ravi Menon: Updated doc with tie-breaker rules and load test plan. Perf target: add <=3ms median latency on resolved path, <=12ms P95 on cold-miss path with signature check. Next: schedule canary with two customers and synthetic traffic.

2025-02-18 - QA (Ana Gomes): Test matrix added to TestRail: streaming passthrough, schema continuation validation, sandbox mode responses. Found one edge case: streaming with interleaved tool outputs that change schema mid-stream — design decision: fail-fast for now and add soft-patch later.
notes: Deliverables: alias engine, admin REST endpoints, redwoodctl UX, canary dashboards, telemetry hooks, security sign-off. Estimated MVE: engine + admin + canary controls in runtime-1.22; follow-ups include UI mapping tool and automated migration assist.
